clue.text: Original clothing

parts.note: the very first garment ever worn, the one Adam and Eve put on in Eden after the Fall

explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis the first humans covered themselves with leaves of the fig tree, so this was the original item of clothing.

clue.text: Coloured musician who had large juvenile following

definitions.note: a relative clause standing for the person it describes

parts.note: pied means of two or more colours, patched like a magpie
a piper is a musician who plays pipes

explanation.surface: A colourful performer once drew a huge crowd of youngsters.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as a description of the whole legend; the charade sits in its first two words, and the rest names the figure.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Hamelin legend the piper, cheated of his fee, led all the town's children away behind him.

clue.text: Game made to leap around

indicators.note: turned around, the letters of these two words are rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone is forced to jump about as part of a game.
explanation.definitionFit: Pelota is a Basque court sport in which a ball is struck against a wall.

clue.text: Offer less for a lot

parts.note: reads like getting a bargain, but means bidding below value for an item at auction or in bridge

explanation.definitionFit: To make a bid lower than an item, or a hand of cards, is worth; a lot is an auction item.

clue.text: Members of the community with no leanings toward crime

definitions.text: Members of the community with no leanings toward crime

parts.words: Members of the community with no leanings toward crime
parts.note: people who stand perfectly straight, not tilting at all, are also honest and law-abiding

explanation.definitionFit: Upright means both vertical and honourable, and citizens are members of a community.

clue.text: On benders, kids err sadly, around the north

definitions.note: a phrase describing people, standing for the people themselves

indicators.note: the scrambled letters go around the abbreviation for north
done sadly, badly, the letters of these two words are jumbled

parts.note: N is the standard abbreviation for north

explanation.surface: Children are making mistakes, gloomily, somewhere up north while out on a spree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sadly' makes DIKSERR from KIDS ERR, and 'around' puts that round N.
explanation.definitionFit: Those out on a drinking spree or binge are heavy imbibers of alcohol.

clue.text: Has a beam moving up and down

definitions.note: a descriptive phrase standing for the device that sends the beam

indicators.note: in a down entry, read upwards or downwards the letters come out the same

parts.note: a descriptive phrase standing for the device that sends the beam

explanation.surface: Something sweeps a ray of light back and forth, like a lighthouse.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is a palindrome: 'moving up and down' says it reads the same either way down the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: This detection system sends out a sweeping radio beam and reads its echoes.

clue.text: Solid piece of ocean field, and shifting!

definitions.text: Solid piece of ocean field, and shifting!

indicators.note: shifting signals that the letters move around: the answer plus the word and rearrange into ocean field

explanation.surface: A frozen chunk floats in an ocean expanse, moving as it goes.
explanation.walkthrough: A composite: the answer's letters together with AND, shuffled ('shifting'), make OCEAN FIELD. Read whole, the clue also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A floe is a flat sheet of floating frozen sea water, a solid piece of the ocean.

clue.text: Apprehend a cleric

explanation.definitionFit: To divine is to grasp by intuition, as in apprehend a truth; a divine is also a clergyman or theologian.

clue.text: Pull up grass on the way back, to feed it?

definitions.text: Pull up grass on the way back, to feed it?

parts.note: to rein in a horse is to pull it up

indicators.note: travelling back means the word for grass is read backwards

parts.note: reed is a tall grass of wetlands

explanation.surface: Someone tugs up grass on their way home to give an animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the way back' turns REED into DEER. Read whole, the clue pictures grass pulled up as the animal's food.
explanation.definitionFit: This Arctic deer grazes on grasses and lichens, so grass is fodder for it.

clue.text: Happy I find crude oil in the plant

parts.note: happy means glad
taken as written

indicators.note: crude, in its rough unrefined sense, tells us these letters are messed about

explanation.surface: A cheerful person strikes crude oil inside a factory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plant' looks like an oil refinery; it is the flower. 'crude' makes OLI from OIL.
explanation.definitionFit: Gladioli are tall flowering plants of the iris family, also called sword lilies.

clue.text: Skirt once could have been man's coat

explanation.definitionFit: A kirtle was an old word for a woman's gown or skirt, and also for a man's tunic or short coat.

clue.text: Islamic official has eaten a second piece of the turtle

indicators.note: the official swallows the letters, so they go inside his title

parts.note: a caliph is a Muslim ruler and religious leader
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Muslim dignitary has dined on a portion of turtle.
explanation.definitionFit: Calipash is the greenish jelly-like meat beneath the upper shell of the turtle, prized in soup.

clue.text: Her heart's broken after departure of a farm worker

indicators.note: broken signals the remaining letters are smashed and rearranged
the letter a has to leave these words before the rearranging

parts.note: the apostrophe-s stands for is, so its S counts as a letter
taken as written

explanation.surface: A woman is heartbroken now a farmhand has left.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after departure of' takes A from HERHEARTS, and 'broken' rearranges what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: A thresher is a person who beats grain from the husks, a traditional job on the land.

clue.text: Food tossed at the pigs

indicators.note: tossed means thrown about, so the letters of these words are scattered

explanation.surface: Scraps are thrown to the hogs in the sty.
explanation.definitionFit: Spaghetti is a kind of pasta, an everyday dish.

clue.text: Flock of frisky lambs? Yes!

indicators.note: frisky, lively and skittish, tells us these letters jump about

explanation.surface: Someone excitedly agrees that the gambolling lambs form a flock.
explanation.definitionFit: An assembly is a gathering of people or creatures, just as a flock is a crowd.

clue.text: Aspiration to do risky manoeuvre on a seaplane

definitions.note: a descriptive phrase standing for the fitted part it describes

parts.note: an aspirate is the breathy sound of the letter H

indicators.note: a manoeuvre is a deft move, so these letters are moved into a new order

explanation.surface: An ambition to perform a dangerous stunt aboard a floatplane.
explanation.definitionFit: A hydroski is a ski-like hydrofoil fitted beneath a seaplane to lift its hull clear of the water at take-off.

clue.text: Shy Eva embarrassed in Jewish school

indicators.note: embarrassed, in its sense of thrown into confusion, means the letters are jumbled

parts.note: the anagram needs an I as well as these six letters

explanation.surface: A timid girl named Eva blushes in her religious school.
explanation.walkthrough: As printed the fodder is one letter short: 'embarrassed' must rearrange SHY EVA plus an I to give the answer, and no clue word supplies the I.
explanation.definitionFit: A yeshiva is an Orthodox institution for studying the Talmud and Torah.

clue.text: Rest ordered, though permitted to fish

indicators.note: ordered, put into a new order, tells us these letters are rearranged

parts.note: permitted means let, as in allowed

explanation.surface: A doctor prescribes rest, but the patient is still allowed to go fishing.
explanation.definitionFit: The sterlet is a small sturgeon of the Caspian and Black Sea region, a source of caviar.

clue.text: Cash required here — ring bell on barrier!

parts.note: to toll is to ring a bell slowly
a gate is a barrier across a way

explanation.surface: A notice tells drivers to pay at the barrier and sound a bell.
explanation.definitionFit: A tollgate is a barrier on a road where a fee must be paid to pass.

clue.text: Sacked, having taken part in a robbery

definitions.text: having taken part in a robbery

explanation.definitionFit: Looted means plundered, as a city is sacked; it also means having stolen goods in a raid.

clue.text: Solid sort of partner for Tristram

indicators.note: sort of signals a loose version, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the anagram needs soiled, which gives the six letters

explanation.surface: A dependable kind of companion for a man named Tristram.
explanation.walkthrough: As held, the clue reads 'Solid', one letter short: the anagram needs SOILED, which 'sort of' turns into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: In Arthurian legend the knight Tristram (Tristan) loved the Irish princess Iseult, also called Isolde.

clue.text: Fate of American plant

parts.note: one's lot is one's fate
US means American

explanation.surface: The destiny of a plant grown in the States.
explanation.definitionFit: The lotus is a water lily, sacred in Asian traditions.

clue.text: Study of animal size from zero to — what a surprise, somehow!

indicators.note: somehow means in some unexplained way, so the letters are arranged anew

parts.note: my! is an exclamation of surprise

explanation.surface: A zoologist's measurements run from nothing up to astonishing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'somehow' rearranges ZERO, TO and MY together.
explanation.definitionFit: Zoometry is the measurement of animals and the proportions of their parts.

clue.text: After a mug of beer, can play bagatelle here

indicators.note: the word for can comes after the word for the mug of beer

parts.note: a pint is a mug of beer
able means can, as in having the ability

explanation.surface: Once you have had a beer, you can have a game in the pub.
explanation.definitionFit: A pintable is a pinball machine, a bagatelle table with pins.

clue.text: Prize going to English second eleven, we hear

indicators.note: we hear says the word for eleven is said aloud and spelt another way

parts.note: a team of eleven, as in cricket or football

explanation.surface: An award goes to an English reserve side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'we hear' turns TEAM into the like-sounding TEEM. In cricket and football a side has eleven players.
explanation.definitionFit: To prize something is to value it highly, to hold it in high regard.

clue.text: Gemstones some travellers see gleaming at night

definitions.text: some travellers see gleaming at night

explanation.definitionFit: Cat's eyes are chatoyant gems such as chrysoberyl; they are also the road-stud reflectors drivers see shining in headlights.
